visual.general_description: Six-panel montage of multi-tracer PET, fused PET/CT and standalone CT for prostate and synchronous sigmoid malignancy.
visual.detailed_description: Panels A and B occupy the upper row; C, D, E and F occupy the lower row. A contains four grayscale PET projections, B four sagittal fused views, C four fused pelvic slices, D and E nine axial fused views each, and F three CT/fused-FAPI pairs. Labels use black panel letters on white patches and yellow tracer names. Uptake appears dark on projection images and red/orange/yellow on fused slices. No numerical chart, axes, uptake scale, SUV values or quantitative measurements are printed. Categories refer to actual displayed acquisitions, distinguishing standalone CT from PET overlays.

panels.general_description: Four labelled whole-body PET maximum-intensity projections.
panels.detailed_description: Top-left block contains four side-by-side grayscale frontal projection images, each showing head, trunk, pelvis and upper legs. Yellow labels along the bottom read PSMA, FDG, DOTATATE and FAPI from left to right. Dark uptake regions differ among projections, with prominent abdominal organ-shaped and central pelvic activity in the PSMA and DOTATATE columns and lighter distributed patterns in FDG and FAPI. Small scattered dark foci are visible at multiple sites. Black dividers separate the images, and the panel letter A is printed at the lower-left. No fused anatomical CT slice is present in this panel.

evidence.quote: Here, we present an interesting case of prostate adenocarcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation (PCND) and signet cell carcinoma sigmoid colon, imaged with four different radiotracers of PET—PSMA, FDG, DOTATATE, and FAPI ( Fig. 1 )—and treated with three cycles of 177 Lu-PSMA RLT ( Fig. 2 ). PCND can present as untreated pathology or more commonly secondary to disease progression as resistance develops to androgen deprivation therapy. PCND can further progress to neuroendocrine prostate carcinoma (NEPC). As NEPCs lose PSMA expression, FDG or SSTR imaging can be used as alternatives.

evidence.quote: At 16 months, he then presented with complaints of lower abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and blood in stool. Colonoscopy revealed an ulcerative lesion 14 cm from the anal verge. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen levels were raised (102.6 ng/mL, normal 0–2.5 ng/mL). Biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma with focal signet ring cell morphology. He was advised for 68 Ga-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor PET/CT ( 68 Ga-FAPI PET/CT) in view of signet ring cell carcinoma. It showed high-grade fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in the heterogeneously enhancing circumferential wall thickening in the sigmoid colon with surrounding serosal irregularity and few tiny pericolonic lymph nodes. Low-grade FAP expression was seen in the known metastatic osteosclerotic lesions from primary prostate malignancy.

limitations: No SUV or CT wall-thickness measurement is printed. Signet-ring histology is source biopsy information, not diagnosed from appearance.
